articles.title: Meta's AI agent Muse lands in the UK in time for Christmas shopping
UK finance watchdog warns AI agent builders they may need a licence

facts.text: Meta's personal AI agent Muse arrived in the UK today, pitched at the festive to-do list.
Unlike Meta AI, which chats and answers questions, Muse connects to other apps and acts: it can build a grocery basket, book a flight, chase a refund, or buy presents.
Sainsbury's lets the agent plan meals and fill grocery orders, while Argos has connected more than 150,000 products, with M&S, Currys, Debenhams and easyJet also on board.
Muse runs as a standalone app, on the web, and inside WhatsApp.
Purchases go through Link, a wallet for AI agents built by Stripe, and buying anything requires the user's approval.
The agent launched in the US in September and ranked first and second on Google's and Apple's free app charts, the Guardian reported.
The Financial Conduct Authority set out its expectations for agentic AI on Tuesday, covering banks, tech providers and social media platforms.
Some personal AI agent products will need FCA authorisation at launch, the regulator warns, and others will grow into needing it later.
Describing a business as a technology provider does not remove the need for authorisation, the regulator says.
On 16 November the UK's four digital regulators wrote to ministers, warning that several personal AI agents are about to launch in the UK.

articles.title: NVIDIA Board Reinstates Jensen Huang as President, CEO and Board Director
Megaspeed, the company at the center of the Jensen Huang scandal, appears headed for a US blacklist

facts.text: The NVIDIA Board of Directors voted unanimously to reinstate Mr. Huang as President and Chief Executive Officer and as a member of the Board, effective immediately.

In the process of reaching its decision, the Board received input from senior levels of the United States government, and based on that input, the Board is confident that Mr. Huang’s reinstatement poses no national security risk.
Harvey Jones will remain as Board chair; the Board is grateful to Colette Kress for her service as interim CEO, in addition to her continuing responsibilities as NVIDIA’s Chief Financial Officer.

The Board formed a committee comprised solely of independent directors to investigate reporting that Mr. Huang has been the target of a foreign intelligence effort; the investigation will proceed to conclusion and Mr. Huang is committed to cooperating.
The Board also formed a National Security and Export Control Committee of independent directors, and NVIDIA is commencing a search to fill a new position, Chief Compliance Officer.
After lobbying from President Trump, Jensen Huang was reinstated as Nvidia CEO on Monday after a short period in which he was ousted by the company’s board.
Megaspeed, which Alice Huang led for over two years, will be added to the Commerce Department’s Entity List, Semafor reported; U.S. companies could not sell to it without a special license.

Megaspeed is a Singapore-based cloud and AI infrastructure provider and was one of Nvidia’s biggest chip customers; the Commerce Department launched a criminal probe last week; the company denies wrongdoing.

stories.title: OpenAI rolls GPT-6.2 Sol into ChatGPT chat
stories.note: Korean-language source (AI타임스, 24 Nov 12:13 KST, quotes OpenAI figures). OpenAI own post not fetched. OpenAI was in 11-23 post (speed limit), -5 if same-company pairing matters. Facts translated.

facts.text: OpenAI began applying GPT-6.2 Sol to ChatGPT general chat on Nov 23 (US time), a version optimized for everyday conversation, introduced earlier this month in Work and Codex.
Image understanding score rose from 47.4% (GPT-6) to 71.7%; complex instruction following from 62.5% to 78.1%; expert-level task score from 52% to 65%.
BrowseComp web-search benchmark at Extra High reasoning: 64.5% versus 54.4% for the previous model.
Compliance with safety policy in sensitive teen conversations: 91-94%, up from 77-80% for GPT-6.
Not every area improved: per the system card, steerability fell from 60.6% to 48.6%.

articles.title: Sierra doubles valuation to $30B within six months as demand for AI in CX takes off

facts.text: Enterprise customer experience company Sierra, co-founded by former Salesforce co-CEO Bret Taylor, raised $1.75 billion in a Series F round that doubles its valuation to $30 billion.
The raise comes within six months of its previous round, which valued the company at $15 billion.
Sierra said it serves almost 50% of Fortune 50 companies; clients include BNY, HSBC, Singtel, Wells Fargo, JPMorganChase, Pearson, Next, and Cox Automotive.
Late last month Sierra said its outcome-based pricing model has helped it double run-rate revenue to $400 million within five months.
Voice AI company ElevenLabs is now valued at $22 billion; Decagon $4.5 billion; Wonderful $5 billion; Parloa $3 billion.
Co-founder Clay Bavor argued at HumanX in Amsterdam in September that a majority of customers are reassigning roles to existing employees rather than replacing humans.

articles.title: Amazon snaps up Decart’s AI optimization tech for $7.5B as it prepares to sell Trainium chips

facts.text: Amazon has agreed to acquire a good chunk of Israeli startup Decart, paying $7.5 billion according to Bloomberg.
Decart builds interactive real-time world models, most recently Oasis 3, and AI video-generation tools.
Decart Optimization Stack (DOS) is software that helps AI models run efficiently on Nvidia, Amazon, and Google’s hardware.
Amazon will acquire the technology behind DOS, plus Decart’s founding team and its team of AI researchers and engineers, Amazon said in a blog post.
Amazon has so far used its Trainium chips at its own data centers and is preparing to start selling them to customers as a competitor to Nvidia.
Peter DeSantis, Amazon SVP: “Every leap forward in AI starts with getting more out of every chip.”

stories.carry_note: TechCrunch only; Reuters version exists but unreadable; price per Bloomberg.

articles.title: Anthropic launches Claude Ship, letting AI agents review, fix, and approve code changes

facts.text: On Monday, the newly public AI company announced Claude Ship, a suite of AI agents for automating code reviews, fixes, and approvals of routine code changes.
It includes an agent that can approve code changes automatically based on policies set by a development team.
Claude Ship consists of Code Review, already generally available, and two new beta agents: PR Steward and Claude Approvals.
PR Steward addresses failing CI checks, merge conflicts, and Code Review feedback, and comments after every push on what it changed and how to roll it back.
Claude Approvals applies an approval policy that the team writes as a file in the repository, in natural language.
Anthropic suggests running the approval functionality in observe-only mode first; teams can start with one repository and set monthly spending limits.
Claude Ship is rolling out to Claude Team and Enterprise plans for repositories on GitHub.
Company blog post: “On the Claude Code team, Claude writes most of our code, and we wanted everything after the PR to move that fast too.”
